description: List the learner's Memrise words for the configured language pair, with the lessons and topics that teach each. To answer questions, filter instead of paging through everything: difficult, learned, known, heard (true or false); due_before (learned words due for review by then, most overdue first when due_before is set; words already known or never studied have no review date and are never included; a plain date YYYY-MM-DD means the end of that day in the learner's time zone, so 'due today' = today's date); topic and lesson (words of a title, any case or accents, e.g. 'food' matches 'Food & Drink'; a topic or lesson that matches nothing adds a warning listing the valid names); min_growth_level, max_growth_level. Filters combine with AND and apply before paging; total counts the matching words. state: 'any' (default) = every word you have met; 'fully_learned_or_known' = only fully learned or already-known words. Returns total, returned and truncated (default limit 200). When truncated is true the result also has next_after_id: call again with after_id set to next_after_id; repeat until truncated is false. If some lesson details cannot be fetched, results are still returned without those lesson links and a `warnings` field names the failed lesson ids. Each word row has word (in the language being learned) and translation (its meaning in the learner's own language). next_review is null unless the word is learned (words never studied, or already known, have none). heard is Memrise's own flag that the word has been heard (its trigger is not documented); heard: true on a word that is not learned or known means only heard, never studied. origin is 'lesson' when a completed or in-progress lesson teaches the word, 'other' when none does (words you have only heard, heard: true, not learned or known, from content outside your lessons; next_review is null so they never look overdue), 'unknown' when none is linked but a lesson failed to load (see warnings); words that are not 'lesson' have no lessons or topics. The first call in a fresh process with a cold cache is noticeably slower because every completed lesson is fetched once; later calls are fast.
name: learnables_list
title: List learner words
